LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.7: Listening for Information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for Information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we listen attentively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information
2. appreciate the roles of extended family members

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for Information helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the roles of extended family members

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the roles of extended family members. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the roles of extended family members.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for Information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the roles of extended family members. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for Information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for Information to a partner. (skill: appreciate the roles of extended family members)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for Information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the roles of extended family members.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for Information from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for Information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Listening for Information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we listen attentively?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for Information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify members of the extended family from an oral text for information.
5. Be able to: appreciate the roles of extended family members.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
